theme: Noun-modifying (relative) clauses — describing a noun with a whole clause
intro: Attach a whole sentence in front of a noun to say things like 'the book I bought' or 'the restaurant my friend recommended.'

grammar.title: Noun-modifying (relative) clauses

rules.label: Clause goes BEFORE the noun
rules.detail: English puts the describing part after the noun; Japanese puts a plain-form clause directly in front of it.
examples: 父が作った料理 → chichi ga tsukutta ryōri (the food my dad made)

rules.label: Verb stays plain form
rules.detail: Use plain form (作った, 読む, 住んでいる), never です/ます, right before the noun.
examples: 昨日泊まったホテル → kinō tomatta hoteru (the hotel I stayed at yesterday)

rules.label: Subject takes が (or の)
rules.detail: The subject inside the clause is marked with が, not は — and casually が often becomes の.
examples: 私が住んでいる町 = 私の住んでいる町 → the town where I live

grammar.bigPoint: No の or 'that' glue between the clause and the noun — the clause sits straight against it, and it can be any tense or polarity (読む本 / 読んだ本 / 読んでいる本 / 読まない本).

examples.jp: これは父が作った料理です。
examples.romaji: Kore wa chichi ga tsukutta ryōri desu.
examples.en: This is the food my father made.

examples.jp: 昨日泊まったホテルはとても静かでした。
examples.romaji: Kinō tomatta hoteru wa totemo shizuka deshita.
examples.en: The hotel I stayed at last night was very quiet.

examples.jp: 友達が勧めた店に行きたいです。
examples.romaji: Tomodachi ga susumeta mise ni ikitai desu.
examples.en: I want to go to the restaurant my friend recommended.

note: Using が (not は) inside the clause keeps the focus on the noun: 田中さんが作った料理 describes the FOOD, while 田中さんは… would start a new sentence about Tanaka. In casual speech that が often turns into の.

selfCheck.q: Say in Japanese: 'The town where I live is small.' (use 住む; 小さい = small)
selfCheck.a: 私が住んでいる町は小さいです。(Watashi ga sunde iru machi wa chiisai desu.) — the clause 私が住んでいる sits right in front of 町. Casual: 私の住んでいる町は小さい。
